title: Subnetting
description: Slicing one network into many smaller ones
tagline: Slicing one network into many smaller ones

sections.title: Why Subnet?
sections.body: Subnetting = cutting one big network into smaller pieces (subnets) by borrowing host bits and turning them into network bits. Why? Smaller broadcast domains, better security between departments, no wasted addresses.

sections.title: The Magic Formula
sections.code:
Subnets created  = 2^borrowed bits
Hosts per subnet = 2^remaining host bits - 2

192.168.1.0/24 -> borrow 2 bits -> /26
  subnets = 2^2 = 4
  hosts   = 2^6 - 2 = 62 per subnet

sections.title: The Block Size Trick
points: Block size = 256 − last interesting mask octet.
Subnets start at 0 and jump by block size: 0, 64, 128, 192...
Last address of a subnet = its broadcast.
First usable = network + 1; last usable = broadcast − 1.
sections.tip: 💡 Practice daily — subnetting speed decides whether you finish the CCNA exam on time!
